question: If you are driving and are 21 years old or older, you are considered to be driving under the influence when your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a minimum of:
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.04 percent.,c:0.06 percent.,d:0.08 percent.
note: A driver with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is driving under the influence. Conviction of driving under the influence may result in a fine, imprisonment, or both.

question: What is the appropriate action to take when approaching a railroad crossing that does not have signals to direct traffic?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
note: When approaching an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be prepared to stop. Before you cross, be sure that no trains are approaching from either direction on any track. If you see or hear a train coming, stop at a safe distance from the nearest track and wait to proceed until after the train passes.

question: What are the colors of signs that tell you the distance to the next exit on a highway?
options: a:Yellow with black letters,b:Black with white letters,c:Red with white letters,d:Green with white letters
note: Signs providing information about destinations are green with white letters or symbols.

question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn into a driveway.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid lines indicate that you may not pass or change lanes. You cannot cross the lines unless it is to turn left to enter or exit a highway, to turn into or from a driveway, or to make a U-turn (where permitted).

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you:
options: a:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,b:Should plan your trip in advance.,c:Only have to know generally where your destination is.
note: When driving to an unfamiliar area, plan your trip in advance. Don’t start with only a hazy idea of where you are going. If your destination is in an unfamiliar area, check the location on a map before you start to drive.

question: Coming to a complete stop at an intersection, yielding to cross traffic/pedestrians, and then proceeding through the intersection when the way is clear corresponds with:
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A solid green light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 mph will result in a fine of ____ for a first offense.
note: Exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 mph will result in a fine of $1,000 for a first-time offense. A second offense will result in a fine of $2,500.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or crossing gates, you should:
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: Always be prepared to yield to any oncoming trains before crossing railroad tracks, particularly if there are no lights or gates controlling the crossing. Never start to cross the tracks until there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side of the tracks. Due to the risk of a vehicle stalling, it is not wise to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks.

question: Defensive driving is:
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: You drive defensively when you identify dangerous driving situations and take action before an accident occurs. Defensive driving helps prevent conflicts with aggressive, offensive, discourteous, careless, inattentive, impulsive, ignorant, or intoxicated drivers or pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic. Drivers must also always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather
note: Crashes often occur when one driver does not see another vehicle or when a driver does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers on the road to help prevent traffic crashes.

question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:
options: a:Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.,b:Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.,c:Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as you can. Bicyclists have much less protection than drivers of motor vehicles and they should not be crowded. Passing a bicycle too quickly can shift the bicyclist off-course.

question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them:
options: a:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:To stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:To run out in front of you without looking.
note: You should always reduce your speed and use extra caution when children are in the vicinity. They may fail to understand the danger and may run out in front of you without looking.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching while displaying flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using a siren, air horn, and/or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Where possible, you must pull over to the right edge of the road. If you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over.

question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
options: a:Excessive stops.,b:Sudden stops.,c:Sudden turns.,d:Excessive speed on wet roads.
note: Your tires become less effective at clearing water from the road as you increase your speed. If you drive too fast, they may lose their grip entirely, leaving the vehicle sliding on a film of water. This is known as "hydroplaning."

question: A load extending more than ____ beyond the rear of a vehicle must be marked by a red flag during the day.
options: a:One foot,b:Two feet,c:Three feet,d:Four feet
note: If a load extends more than four feet past the rear of a vehicle, it must be marked by a red flag when being transported during the day in clear weather. The flag should be 18 inches square. Red lights and reflectors are required when transporting the load in times of limited visibility.

question: A diamond-shaped sign:
options: a:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of existing or potential driving hazards. You will usually see these signs in yellow or orange.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: One strategy to avoid driving while impaired or intoxicated is to arrange for a ride home with a friend who does not drink. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower cannot reduce your blood alcohol content or reduce the effects of alcohol. On average, it takes about an hour for the body to eliminate the alcohol from a single drink.

question: Drivers must have a minimum of ____ in both Personal Injury Protection (PIP) insurance coverage and Property Damage Liability (PDL) insurance coverage.
note: According to Florida's No-Fault Law, every owner or person in charge of operating a motor vehicle in Florida must provide proof of valid PIP and PDL insurance at the time of vehicle registration. They must have a minimum of $10,000 in PIP coverage and a minimum of $10,000 in PDL coverage.

question: At a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: You must always yield to pedestrians who are in or about to enter a crosswalk. Be alert to pedestrians when driving across intersections or turning.

question: What is a "No zone?"
options: a:A designated no passing zone,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle
note: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and other large vehicles. Drivers of smaller vehicles should avoid lingering in "No zones."

question: When meeting a car with blinding headlights, you should:
options: a:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,c:Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
note: If a vehicle comes toward you with its high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car has passed. This will keep you from being blinded.

question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants in to the left. That shows that:
options: a:There is an intersection just ahead.,b:You are approaching a construction area.,c:You will be required to turn left just ahead.
note: A solid line along the side of the road indicates where its edge is, marking the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. If the edge line angles toward the center of the road, this means that the road is narrower ahead.

question: When driving on roads that may be slippery:
options: a:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Reduce your following distance.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: You should avoid making any sudden changes in speed or direction when driving on a slippery surface. Reduce your speed on slippery roads and do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: When you park on a downward-facing slope, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. This way, if your vehicle starts to roll downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

question: Downward-facing triangular signs:
options: a:Indicate school zones.,b:Tell drivers to yield.,c:Indicate construction zones.
note: Downward-facing triangular signs usually indicate that drivers should yield. Once the road is clear of traffic or pedestrians and it is safe to do so, drivers may proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop:
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At four-way stops, traffic from all four directions must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection should move forward first. If two vehicles reach the intersection at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: The risk of hydroplaning can can be reduced by driving:
options: a:Through shallow water.,b:More quickly.,c:More slowly.
note: Because hydroplaning is caused by driving too quickly in wet conditions, the risk of it happening can be reduced by driving more slowly.

question: When getting ready to change lanes, you should:
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Check your rearview mirror.,c:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.
note: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic approaching you from behind. Just before you begin moving into the other lane, quickly glance over your shoulder and check for any vehicles that may be in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Speed up.,b:Go the same speed.,c:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete the pass easily.
note: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should slow down so that there is enough room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete their pass. This will allow them to complete the passing maneuver in less time and more easily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection and no markings appear to indicate a stop line or crosswalk, a driver:
options: a:Is not required to stop.,b:Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.,c:Should stop only at a place where they can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if they have to enter the intersecting roadway.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you should stop at the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you can get a view of approaching traffic. You should not enter the intersecting roadway to gain a better view.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you should look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop for trains or other vehicles that may be using the rails.

question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.
note: When passing, you must always signal at least 100 feet in advance of your lane change. Always check behind you in your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.

question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:
options: a:Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.,b:Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.,c:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.
note: To prevent hydroplaning, you should ensure that the tires on your vehicle have good tread depth and are inflated to the proper pressure. Reduce the speed of your vehicle when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning occurs most frequently at higher speeds.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow,b:Single broken yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-way road means that it is prohibited for traffic from either direction to cross the center to pass.

question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch out for standing water or puddles.
note: When roads are wet, cars take a longer distance to stop and may skid on quick turns. Do not use cruise control when driving under wet or icy conditions. Reduce your speed and drive with caution.

question: If worried, nervous, angry, or crying, a driver:
options: a:Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.,b:Can drive faster because they are more in touch with their senses.,c:Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
note: You may not be able to drive well if you are worried, excited, crying, angry, or depressed. Emotions can distract you from your driving because your mind is focused on something else. Take time to calm down and get focused before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:
options: a:Has the right-of-way.,b:Should yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:May force their way into traffic.
note: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you should yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely into traffic when you are able to do so.

question: Alcohol causes:
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.
note: Consuming even a small amount of alcohol will impair your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: A driver who is taking a non-prescription drug should:
options: a:Read the labels on the drug before driving.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive safely. If you take medication, even a remedy for colds or allergies that is not prescribed, check the label for warnings about its effects. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist about driving while on the medication.

question: The most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash are:
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Safety belts can double your chance of surviving a crash and more than double your chance of avoiding serious injury. Airbags, when used properly with safety belts, provide additional protection in a front-end crash. You should wear both shoulder and lap belts.

question: Seat belts are most effective when they are worn by:
options: a:The person driving the car.,b:Passengers when they are on a long drive.,c:All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.
note: When you drive, make sure each person in your vehicle wears a seat belt. In the event of a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and a danger to each person in the vehicle.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing that has no visible gates or flashing lights, but has a standard crossbuck. You should:
options: a:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know that there is no train coming.,b:Turn your radio down to hear if there may be an approaching train.,c:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger, if applicable.
note: You must approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you know that no train is coming from either direction. If there is a flagger at a crossing, you must obey all of their instructions.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:
options: a:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs are used to warn drivers of the possibility of a train. Drivers should obey all railroad crossing warning signs and never go around barriers or disregard the warning sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn. You should:
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes. You should keep your wheels straight while waiting to make a left turn. If another vehicle hits you from behind, this ensures that you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When should you drive in a lane under a lane signal showing a red X?
options: a:If there is no visible oncoming traffic.,b:If you are passing the car in front of you.,c:Between sunset and sunrise.
note: Lane use control signals are used when the direction of the flow of traffic in a specific lane changes throughout the day. They are used to show which lanes of traffic are open and closed, as well as to show if toll booths are open or closed. Drivers should never drive in a lane underneath a red X.

question: You are coming to a railroad crossing where the crossing signals are flashing. You should:
options: a:Stop and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Look for a train, then speed up.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop your vehicle no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail if an installed electric or mechanical signal is giving warning of an approaching train. Be aware of other warning signs that may indicate an oncoming train, including seeing a lowered crossing gate or hearing an oncoming train.

question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:Signal a lane change.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,c:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
note: Any time you want to change lanes, you should properly signal your intentions well in advance, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. You can check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder in the direction that you plan to move.

question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Your blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. It is not affected by the type of alcoholic beverages you drink, your level of physical fitness, or how well you can "hold your liquor."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle:
options: a:In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.,b:By using the shoulder of the highway.,c:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
note: You may not pass another vehicle on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may cause a collision. Never pass another vehicle by driving onto the shoulder of a highway. Passing another vehicle by driving over a solid yellow line is prohibited.

question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Use alternate routes.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads, you should increase your following distance. It may take more time to stop your vehicle than it would under normal conditions.

question: A driver should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:
options: a:They’re difficult to see in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: In many collisions with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians, drivers reported that they were looking but still did not see the smaller vehicle or pedestrian. These can be more difficult to spot in traffic than passenger vehicles because they are smaller, may move faster, and have less noticeable lighting. To prevent collisions with these smaller and less protected road users, drivers should always be alert to the presence of motorcycles, bikes, and pedestrians.

question: You are driving along a street and hear a siren. You cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle. You should:
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.,c:Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
note: If you hear a siren or an air horn close by but do not know exactly where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted speed limit shows:
options: a:Only a recommended driving speed.,b:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal driving speed for the stretch of highway where it is posted. Driving safely may require you to travel more slowly than the posted limit. When conditions are less than ideal, drivers should slow down.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:
options: a:Warns you about conditions on or near the road.,b:Helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.,c:Tells you about traffic laws and regulations.
note: Warning signs, which tell you about conditions on or near the road ahead, are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a road with two lanes traveling in opposite directions, you should:
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane roadway, you must return to the right side of the roadway when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you have passed.

question: Flashing hazard lights may be used:
options: a:When your vehicle is stopped or disabled on the highway or shoulder.,b:When rain decreases visibility.,c:When driving at night.
note: Flashing hazard lights must only be used if your vehicle is disabled or legally stopped on the highway or shoulder. They may also be used when driving in a funeral procession.

question: You are involved in an accident and another person is injured. You should:
options: a:Moved the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily. Keep the injured warm and administer first aid.
note: After an accident, do not move the injured unnecessarily. Unskilled handling can make serious injuries out of minor ones. Keep the injured warm until skilled help arrives. If there is severe bleeding, attempt to stop the flow of blood with direct pressure.

question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
options: a:Flat.,b:Curvy.,c:In the sun.,d:Shaded by trees or buildings.
note: In cold or wet weather, you should take special care on sections of road that are shaded by trees or buildings. These areas freeze more quickly than the rest of the road and are the last parts of the road to dry.

question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before getting behind the wheel:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that negatively affects judgment, vision, concentration, understanding of reality, and reaction time. It is never safe to consume alcohol in any amount before getting behind the wheel of a car.

question: An octagonal sign is always a:
options: a:Speed limit sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Hospital sign.
note: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when approaching a red, eight-sided sign.

question: When you see a "Drawbridge" sign and you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Quickly speed up.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: When a yellow light is flashing near a drawbridge, the drawbridge is in operation. Slow down and prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower-moving vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Not cross the centerline.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.,c:Use the shoulder.,d:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires good judgment because you must use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if you may safely and legally do so.

question: On the freeway, you see a "Merging traffic“ sign. You should:
options: a:Honk at incoming traffic.,b:Always remain at your present speed.,c:Speed up to avoid congesting traffic.,d:Move over one lane to make room for entering vehicles.
note: When on a roadway with two or more lanes, you should make room for entering vehicles. If there is no one driving next to you, move over one lane.

question: When a drawbridge signal is red, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Quickly speed up.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: If a drawbridge signal is red, come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. The bridge is in operation and the roadway is closed to all pedestrian and motor vehicle traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, it is important to:
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When you have completed the turn, your car should be:
options: a:In the right lane of the street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the street.
note: If you are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you have just left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers:
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
note: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians who are on an intersecting sidewalk.

question: Under normal weather and traffic conditions, keep a minimum following distance of:
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.,d:Four seconds.
note: The more distance between your vehicle and others, the more time you have to react to potential hazards. Keep a minimum following distance of four seconds under normal weather and traffic conditions. Increase your following distance during unusual weather or traffic conditions.

question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle is not equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: Pumping the brakes is generally the best way to stop a car in an emergency. The car will stop quickly and you will also be able to continue steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic. You may receive a citation for driving too slowly.

question: Round signs indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round signs warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing area. Drivers should use extra caution when approaching a railroad crossing.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:
options: a:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,b:Look both ways as you cross the intersection.,c:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
note: A triangular red and white yield sign means that you must decrease speed as you approach an intersection and yield the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection. You must be prepared to stop if conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From the center lane, which maneuver(s) can you perform?
options: a:You may make left turns.,b:You may make U-turns.,c:You may pass slow-moving traffic.
note: This sign indicates where a lane is reserved for the exclusive use of left-turning vehicles from either direction. Such a lane may not be used for passing or for through-traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop.
note: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, they are indicating that they intend to stop. Adjust your driving accordingly if following a driver who is using this hand signal.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means that passing is not permitted from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Either one,b:The vehicle on the left,c:The vehicle on the right
note: At intersections that are controlled by signs or signals and at intersections that are uncontrolled, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right when two vehicles arrive to the intersection at the same time.

question: As a pedestrian, you should:
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the vehicle driver’s responsibility to stop.
note: Pedestrians should not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle approaching from a close distance may not have the time to stop before entering the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The speed limit is ____ in school zones.
options: a:55 mph,b:45 mph,c:30 mph,d:20 mph
note: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Use extra caution when driving in school zones.

question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.,d:Come to a complete stop.
note: A steady red traffic light indicates that drivers must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is against the law and is extremely dangerous. Drivers may turn right on a steady red light if there is no sign prohibiting a turn on red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: Don’t make a last-minute turn into an exit. If you pass your exit, you must go to the next one.

question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
options: a:Communicate with other road users.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: Crashes often happen because one driver does something that other road users are not expecting. You should communicate with other motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians by doing things like signaling when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when appropriate.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky behavior that puts not only you and your passengers in danger, but also endangers pedestrians, bicyclists, and other motorists sharing the road. Focused attention on driving helps to prevent crashes.

question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgement of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol reduces your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, changes your judgment of speed and distances, reduces your ability to recover from the glare of headlights, and often reduces your inhibitions and makes you more likely to take risks.

question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
options: a:Signal lights.,b:Other cars on the road.,c:The time of day.,d:The condition of the road.
note: Your ability to stop is greatly affected by the condition of the road. You need to reduce your speed when road conditions are poor in order to maintain control of your vehicle. You will be at risk if you are driving too quickly on roads that are slippery and you need to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A speed limit is:
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions. You may drive more slowly than the posted speed, but it is illegal to drive any faster. You must drive more slowly where signs or signs indicate a school zone or work zone speed limit. If conditions such as road construction or bad weather make the posted speed unsafe, drive under the speed limit.

question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:
options: a:The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.,b:That due to upcoming roadwork, there is a detour to the right.,c:Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
note: This sign indicates that the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle (in this case, to the right). Before you reach such an extreme curve, you should slow down as much as you would when making a turn at an intersection.

question: When encountering an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Retaliate by tailgating them.
note: If another driver is threatening you or intentionally driving dangerously around you, remain calm and try to put as much distance between the two of you as possible. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact and do not make obscene gestures.

question: You should be cautious when passing a bicycle because:
options: a:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
note: You should always be cautious when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always be particularly careful when driving near bicyclists.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
note: You should not use cruise control on snow, in rain, in fog, or under similar hazardous conditions. Winter is the most difficult driving season and requires extra caution from drivers. It is important to consistently check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels. Using snow tires can increase a vehicle's traction on the surface of slippery roads.

question: You may cross solid yellow lines:
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:During daylight hours only.,c:At any time.
note: As a general rule, broken traffic lines may be crossed but solid lines may not. Solid yellow lines may be crossed only when the driver is making a turn.

question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second approaching train after one train passes. Do not begin to cross the tracks until you’re sure no train is approaching from either direction on either track.

question: Work zone signs mean:
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.
note: Work zone signs are orange and indicate that some type of work is being performed on or alongside the roadway. Be extremely careful when you see these signs.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway following a stop, you must:
options: a:Honk to let them know you’re there.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Yield.
note: You must yield to any transit vehicle that is signaling to pull back onto the main roadway after it has stopped to load or unload passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to allow the bus safe re-entry into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Leaving the scene of a crash is:
options: a:Encouraged.,b:The most efficient way to handle an accident.,c:Not recommended, but is acceptable.
note: It is against the law to leave the scene of a crash that causes property damage, injury, or death. Drivers involved in such an accident are required to provide their information and supply aid.

question: Guide signs are ____ signs that provide directional and mileage information to drivers.
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide signs, sometimes known as destination signs, have a green background and provide directional and mileage information to specific destinations. They can be a helpful resource when driving in unfamiliar locations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum or minimum safe speed that is allowed to be driven on a roadway. The maximum limits are for ideal conditions and you must reduce your speed when conditions require it.

question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop, unless they are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow traffic light indicates that a red light is about to appear. Stop unless you are already within the intersection.

question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.
options: a:The funeral procession,b:A pedestrian,c:Another driver
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield the right-of-way to funeral processions. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the remaining vehicles in the funeral procession may follow through the intersection regardless of any traffic control devices.

question: When driving on slick roads, you should:
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Accelerate quickly.
note: While it is always dangerous to drive too fast on slippery roads, this is especially true when driving in turns and curves. Be sure to approach them more slowly in slippery conditions than you would under normal circumstances.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to:
options: a:Get some coffee.,b:Open your window.,c:Stop driving.
note: Being fatigued while driving is similar in danger to driving under the influence of alcohol. If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to stop driving.

question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Turning left or right.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot every time you want to change your vehicle's position. If you are turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb, you should check your blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do not pass:
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When school bus lights are flashing.,c:When approaching an intersection.
note: You should never pass if there is an oncoming vehicle in the passing lane, if your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any other no passing zone. Unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane roadway with a median or shared center turn lane, you may not pass a stopped school bus that has its flashing red lights activated.

question: If you need to drive in foggy weather:
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: You are required to use your headlights during the day when visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less. When you first turn on your headlights, be sure they are adjusted to the low beam setting. Using high beams in fog or rain will cause the light to reflect back into your eyes, lowering visibility even more.

question: You come to an intersection displaying a flashing red light. You should:
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,c:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
note: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as a stop sign. You must stop, yield the right-of-way, and go once it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but you are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make your turn then.
note: Never make last-minute turns. If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but you are not in the proper lane to make the turn, drive to the next intersection and then make the turn from the proper lane.

question: On a road which has no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:
options: a:Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.,b:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic in the lane nearest them.

question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:
options: a:Not put too much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.,b:Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.,c:Disregard any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.,d:Take a few minutes to familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls.
note: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the location and operation of the turn signals, hazard warning signals, headlights and beam selector, windshield wipers and washers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Any defects should be corrected before the vehicle is driven.

question: A yellow light that flashes on and off means:
options: a:Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means drivers should slow down and proceed with caution.

question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can,b:Alcohol does not,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
note: Even the smallest amount of alcohol will reduce your concentration, perception, judgment and memory, and your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

question: A driver who has been convicted of three traffic offenses that caused accidents over the course of three years:
options: a:Must complete a DHSMV-approved driver improvement course.,b:Must hand in their license.,c:Will not be permitted to drive on freeways.
note: The Three Crashes in Three Years Law requires drivers who have been convicted of three traffic incidents that have caused accidents over the course of 36 months to enroll in and complete an approved driver improvement course. The driver must also complete behind-the-wheel training from a commercial driving school and pass an extended driving test. The requirements must be met within 90 days or the driver's license will be canceled.

question: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means that passing is allowed from the lane on the side next to the broken line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: Driving more slowly than the flow of traffic can be hazardous. If you are on a two-lane, two-way road and driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you are required to pull off the road and let the other vehicles pass. Only drive significantly under the speed limit when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Yield to pedestrians.
note: Unless a posted sign prohibits it, you may turn right or left at a steady green light. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians within the intersection.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic light means that:
options: a:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.,c:A driver must stop and then proceed when the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
note: Unless a posted sign indicates otherwise, a traffic signal displaying a red arrow means that drivers must come to a full stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

question: You are driving on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines. You may:
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles, but only if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Cross these lines under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines are used to mark roadways where passing is prohibited from both directions. You may cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

question: A regulatory sign containing a red circle with a slash through the middle indicates:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: Some regulatory signs prohibit certain actions. These signs are rectangular and white with red and black markings. A red circle and slash on top of a black symbol indicates that the specified action is forbidden.

question: You must pull over to the edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass:
options: a:Regardless of your direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, regardless of whether it is approaching you from behind or from the opposite direction.

question: On a two-lane street, your vehicle is being followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals. You should:
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If you are being followed by an emergency vehicle that is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to clear a path. Continue driving in a normal manner.

question: Which is not a factor in determining the distance that it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability,b:Braking distance,c:Reaction distance
note: The distance required to stop your vehicle depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. This changes with speed and road conditions.

question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and severity of crashes.
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night drives
note: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and severity of crashes. The faster you drive, the greater the impact or striking power of your vehicle, should you be involved in a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is ____ in municipal, business, and residential areas.
options: a:70 mph,b:55 mph,c:45 mph
note: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in municipal, business, or residential areas is 30 mph. If a posted sign indicates otherwise, follow the speed limit on the posted sign.

question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle goes into a skid, you should turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. As soon as the vehicle begins to straighten out, turn the steering wheel back the other way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you are going to enter a roadway from a private road?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.,b:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.,c:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.,d:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already on the public road.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.,c:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: You must do everything you can to prevent striking a pedestrian or another vehicle, regardless of the circumstances. It is the driver’s basic responsibility to be alert to pedestrians and to yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing the street where they should not be.

question: Posters, signs, and stickers on the windshield and windows:
options: a:Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.,b:Are permitted if they allow the driver at least a little visibility.,c:Are prohibited, unless they are otherwise specifically required by law.
note: Obstructions on windows are prohibited. No sign, poster, or sticker may be placed on any window of a vehicle, unless it is specifically required by law to be on a vehicle's window.

question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, it is a good idea to:
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Drive with one eye open at a time.
note: To avoid becoming fatigued while taking a long trip, stop every two hours for a short break. If you become drowsy, pull off the road and park in a safe place to take a nap, or find a room to stay for the night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a stop sign, you should stop and:
options: a:Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.,b:Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.,c:Look right first, then left, then right again.
note: When stopped at an intersection, you should first look to your left, as vehicles coming from the left are closer to you than vehicles coming from the right. Look to your right, then look to your left again, in case there are any vehicles coming from that direction that you did not see at first glance.

question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Allergy medicine,b:Marijuana,c:Cold remedies
note: Many kinds of drugs can impair your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. It can be a criminal offense to drive while impaired by any drug.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A good rule to remember for passing is:
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,c:Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.
note: Each time you pass another vehicle, there is an increased chance for a collision. If you are moving faster than surrounding traffic, you will have to continue passing others. Drive with the flow of traffic, within the legal speed limit, and pass only as needed.

question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
options: a:Are making a turn.,b:Have your emergency brake on.,c:Are changing lanes.,d:Are slowing down or stopping.
note: Your vehicle's brake lights indicate to other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights should always be in working order when you are driving on any roadway.

question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light indicates that a steady red light will soon appear. If you are driving toward an intersection and a yellow light appears, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already within the intersection or cannot stop safely before entering the intersection, continue through carefully.

question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. You should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.,c:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.
note: When changing lanes, you should check your vehicle's blind spots by looking over your shoulder in the direction that you want to move. Always check your mirrors and turn on your directional signal before beginning a lane change.

question: Curbs painted yellow indicate:
options: a:Designated free parking areas.,b:Paid parking areas.,c:No parking zones.
note: Some restricted parking areas are designated by painted curbs. Curbs painted yellow may indicate a loading zone, a fire hydrant, or other restrictions prohibiting parking.

question: What is the first thing you should adjust, if needed, when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat belt,b:The steering wheel,c:Your rearview mirror
note: When preparing to drive, you should first adjust your seat to ensure that you are in a comfortable position and can see the road clearly. Adjust your mirrors and steering wheel to be effective when your seat is fully adjusted.

question: When changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.
note: Other cars and motorcycles are often hidden in a vehicle’s blind spot, so be sure to glance over your shoulder before you begin a lane change. Begin signaling 100 feet before changing lanes or turning in a residential area. Signal five seconds in advance when changing lanes on a freeway.

question: Signs that are colored orange are:
options: a:Work zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:School zone signs.
note: Highway work zones are established according to the type of work underway along the roadway. Signs in work areas are typically diamond-shaped, orange, have black letters or symbols, and serve as a warning that people are working on or near the highway.

question: If another car is in danger of hitting you, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Wave your arms.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: Your horn should be used to warn other drivers or pedestrians in situations where they may not see you. For example, if you think another driver is about to hit you, you should sound your horn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Fines for moving traffic violations in construction zones are:
options: a:Lessened.,b:Doubled.,c:Unchanged.
note: In Florida, fines are doubled when infractions occur within construction zones. There will also be possible civil penalties of up to $1,000 and you can be required to complete a driving school course.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Solid white lines are used to separate lanes traveling in the same direction (as well as to mark the right edge of the road). Broken white lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and may be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
note: Special child seats are available for children who are too small to wear regular safety belts. No person is strong enough to safely hold onto a child of any size during an accident or sudden stop. Never allow a child to ride in a vehicle unless they are properly fastened into a seat.

question: What are the colors of warning signs indicating upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a white background,b:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background,c:White letters or symbols on a blue background
note: Warning signs that indicate approaching hazards are usually yellow with black lettering or symbols. Warning signs in work zones are orange with black lettering or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:
options: a:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
note: When using a freeway exit ramp, do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
options: a:Road hazard sign.,b:Interstate route sign.,c:School crossing sign.
note: Warning signs are normally diamond-shaped and yellow, although orange warning signs are used in work areas. Such signs warn that you are approaching a hazardous location or an area where special rules apply.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
note: Because of their size, trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway, you should signal before carefully exiting the roadway and turning on your hazard flashers. Get as far off the road as possible and park in a location where other drivers can easily see you. Lift your hood to let other drivers know your vehicle is disabled.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue driving when they think most kids are probably done exiting the bus.
note: When approaching a stopped school bus that is using its stop signal, a driver is required to come to a complete stop. They should not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: You should honk your horn when you:
options: a:Are traveling through an intersection.,b:Are passing a bicyclist.,c:See a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Your horn should be used as a warning in situations where you think another driver or a pedestrian does not see you. For example, if a child begins to run into the street in front of your vehicle, you should sound your horn.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines are used to separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines indicate that drivers are not permitted to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:
options: a:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,c:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to any approaching vehicles or crossing pedestrians. The stop should be made before crossing the sidewalk area. Failure to stop is unlawful.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line in the center of a road indicates that vehicles traveling in both directions are permitted to pass. Drivers may only begin a pass if they will not interfere with any oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. You should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
note: Keep right when another driver begins to pass you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to let the passing vehicle move back into the right lane as easily as possible.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic that are moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines may be crossed to pass or change lanes, if it is safe to do so.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means that you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with care.,b:Continue normally through the intersection.,c:Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
note: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means "caution." If you approach such a light, slow down, look, and proceed with care.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:
options: a:Maintain their speed and proceed.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Yield to all other drivers.
note: At an intersection where there is no stop sign or traffic signal, you should yield to a vehicle approaching the intersection from the right. However, always be prepared to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by taking your foot off the accelerator, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

question: When driving past a vehicle that has just stopped in a parked position on the side of the road, you should:
options: a:Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.,b:Speed up.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: When passing a vehicle that has just parked parallel to the road, you should assume the driver will open the door as you approach. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, drivers must stop within ____ of the first rail, when indicated to do so.
options: a:70 feet,b:50 feet,c:15 feet
note: Any driver or pedestrian approaching a railroad crossing must stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet, from the nearest rail of the railroad when warning lights are flashing, crossing gates are lowered, or drivers are otherwise instructed to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning onto a street with more than one lane traveling in your direction, you should:
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,c:Turn into the middle lane.
note: When turning onto a street with more than one lane moving in the direction that you are traveling, turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes when turning.

question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System starts to lose traction on a slippery road, drivers should:
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: If their vehicle loses traction on a slippery road, a driver with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) needs to press down hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer out of danger. In an emergency situation, the ABS automatically pumps the brakes at a faster rate than the driver could. Removing steady pressure from the brake pedal or pumping the brakes will disengage the ABS.

question: A leaky exhaust system in your vehicle is dangerous because it can cause:
options: a:A loss of hearing.,b:Pollution.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: The exhaust system carries exhaust gas out of the vehicle and prevents fumes from entering into the passenger compartment. To prevent carbon monoxide poisoning, keep your exhaust system free of leaks. Replace all defective parts immediately.

question: If you are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using its flashing lights approaches your vehicle, you must:
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: If an emergency vehicle using its lights or siren approaches while you are driving on a one-way street, you must drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.

question: What do lane signals with a yellow X indicate?
options: a:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:Drivers may drive normally in this lane.
note: Lane use control signals are used when the direction of the flow of traffic in a specific lane changes throughout the day. They are used to show which lanes of traffic are open and closed, as well as to show if toll booths are open or closed. When a lane signal contains a yellow X, drivers should clear the indicated lane, as the lane signal is about to change to a red X.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger.,b:It is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign. Stop when flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals, and signs. These devices inform drivers of conditions on the roadway and help guide drivers safely to their destinations. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
note: Consuming alcohol and other drugs together can increase the impairing effects of both. For example, having one drink while you are also using a cold remedy could affect you as much as several drinks would when being consumed separately from any medications.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate:
options: a:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,b:You should always use cruise control.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder of the interstate in the case of an emergency and change lanes as infrequently as possible. Cruise control should not be used in heavy traffic or under poor weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: Your turn signals should always be used when you make any movement to the left or right. You should use your signal when pulling into traffic from a curbside parking space, moving into a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The driver,c:Whoever is slower
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians when they are crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you’re going to turn left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The right lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Either lane.
note: You should always turn from the lane that is closest to the direction you want to go. Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.

question: You are driving when it begins to rain. You should:
options: a:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,b:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,c:Slow down.
note: When heavy rain reduces visibility, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle. If the rain is so heavy that you are unable to see clearly, drive onto the shoulder and stop until the rain lets up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A “No stopping” sign means that, unless directed to do so by a police officer, you may stop only:
options: a:Long enough to unload packages.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,c:To discharge passengers.
note: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, to obey a police officer, or to prevent a conflict with another vehicle.

question: Larger vehicles have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have spots close to their rears that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

question: Which of the following best ensures your safety and the safety of those around you when you are backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
note: Backing requires extra caution because it is difficult for drivers to see behind their vehicles. Before entering a vehicle to back up, walk to the back of the vehicle to check for children and small objects.

question: Florida law requires you to use headlights:
options: a:To get the attention of vehicles surrounding you.,b:During a clear day.,c:Between sunset and sunrise.
note: Florida law says that you must use headlights when driving between sunset and sunrise. Drive with extra care when driving at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from multilane, one-way streets and highways, you should start from:
options: a:The middle of the intersection.,b:The right lane.,c:The left lane.
note: To turn left from multilane streets and highways, start from the left lane.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Do not drive in someone else’s blind spot. Move forward or drop back so that the other driver can see you.

question: Pentagonal signs indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate that you are in a school zone. Be extra alert to children and pedestrians when driving near a school.

question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on the:
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign.,c:Use of your turn signals.
note: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

question: Emergency vehicles:
options: a:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,b:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.,c:May follow each other.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, or any other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn and a red or blue flashing light. Follow any instructions given over the emergency vehicles' loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other so you should proceed only when you are certain the way is clear.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When you see an emergency vehicle using its lights or hear it using its siren, you must immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

question: If you pass a school bus that is stopped to drop off or pick up children, you will:
options: a:Be fined at least $265.,b:Be fined less than $100.,c:Not be fined, but your license will be suspended.
note: Drivers must come to a complete stop when approaching a school bus that is stopped with its lights flashing. Failure to stop until the lights stop flashing will result in a fine of at least $265. Passing a bus on the side where its door is located will result in a fine of at least $465. Additional penalties will apply.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the left lane and a vehicle behind you is operating at a higher speed:
options: a:It is your right to continue using the left lane.,b:You are required by law to move out of the left lane.,c:You should ignore the other vehicle.
note: Florida Law states that a driver must move out of the left lane when being overtaken from behind by another vehicle traveling at a higher rate of speed. Safely merge into a different lane.
