question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines indicate that drivers are not permitted to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Come to a stop.
note: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, they are indicating that they intend to turn right. Adjust your driving accordingly if following a driver who is using this hand signal.

question: You may honk your horn when you:
options: a:Have to stop quickly.,b:Are passing another car.,c:Have lost control of your car.
note: One situation where it is appropriate to use your horn is if you lose control of your vehicle. In this case, sound your horn to alert other drivers.

question: This green arrow on a lane use control signal means:
options: a:You may use this lane.,b:No traffic is allowed in this lane.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: A steady downward green arrow over a traffic lane means you may use the lane indicated.

question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:
options: a:Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.,b:Dangerous.,c:Safe locations to park a car.
note: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Drivers should always look and listen for trains approaching from either direction on all railroad tracks. Always follow the directions indicated by signs, signals, and flaggers. Never proceed past a railroad crossing until you are certain it is safe to do so.

question: Which of the following is true regarding seat belts and child restraints in vehicles?
options: a:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,c:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.
note: Before you drive, always fasten your seat belt and make sure all your passengers are using seat belts or child restraints. Studies have shown that if you use seat belts, your chances of being hurt or killed in a traffic crash are greatly reduced. Children age 12 and under should always ride properly restrained in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front passenger airbag.

question: Road rage and aggressive driving may be reduced by:
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.
note: As an increasing number of drivers populate the roadways, road rage becomes more prevalent. To help prevent road rage, a driver should use proper turn signals, obey posted speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

question: What should you do if your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement?
options: a:Stop quickly.,b:Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.,c:Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.,d:Slow down and ease back onto the roadway.
note: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, don’t panic. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the roadway by keeping both hands on the steering wheel and steering into the road’s right lane with a small turn of the steering wheel. Check for traffic around you before steering back onto the pavement.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.,c:Make you drowsy while driving.
note: The exhaust system helps remove toxic gases, reduce the noise, and cool the hot gases coming from a running engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system can cause death in a very short time. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

question: A telltale sign of a drunk driver is:
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:They are making quick and sudden stops.
note: Telltale signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow, making jerking motions, and making quick and sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to get off the freeway but you have missed your exit, you should:
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit, you should take the next exit. Do not stop or back up on the highway, swerve across multiple lanes to try to make the exit at the last second, or cross over the median to turn around. All of these maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:
options: a:A deaf person.,b:A person involved with a traffic study.,c:A blind person.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian when the pedestrian is a blind person who is using a white cane or guide dog.

question: Stress can affect your driving by:
options: a:Lowing your ability to focus on driving.,b:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,c:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Emotions can have a great effect on your driving ability. You may not be able to drive well if you are overly worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad. Stress can lessen your concentration on the task of driving. It is better to wait to drive than to risk driving while you are emotionally unstable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning, you should:
options: a:Use your signal.,b:Turn the wheel.,c:Increase your speed.
note: To complete a turn safely, you should activate your turn signal three to four seconds before your turn.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious traffic safety problem. Safe driving is not possible when you drink alcohol or take other drugs. Driving under the influence is dangerous both to you and to others on the road.

question: The consumption of alcohol while taking drugs can:
options: a:Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:Help cure your illness.
note: The combination of alcohol and drugs, in some cases, can increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol. It can be unsafe to drive after consuming either alcohol or drugs and is even more dangerous after combining them.

question: Low beam headlights are effective for vehicles driving at speeds of up to:
options: a:10 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:50 mph.
note: Low beam headlamps are only effective when driving at speeds of up to 20 to 25 mph. Avoid driving too fast for what you can see within your headlamps.

question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: When approaching an intersection with a solid yellow traffic light, slow to a stop before entering the intersection, if it is safe to do so. If you can't stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Anything makes conditions less than perfect.,b:You see a police car.,c:Entering a highway where there are other cars.
note: When the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect, drive below the posted speed limit. Even if you are driving within the posted speed limit, you can still be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is ____ on limited-access highways.
options: a:70 mph,b:55 mph,c:45 mph
note: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on limited-access highways is 70 mph. If a posted sign indicates otherwise, follow the speed limit on the posted sign.

question: An approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, glance toward the right side of the road. This will keep you from being blinded by the other vehicle’s headlights and will allow you to see enough of the road to stay on course until the other vehicle has passed.

question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:
options: a:May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.,b:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:Still have the right-of-way to turn.
note: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you may still turn in the direction that the arrow was pointing but you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A red flashing traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign. When approaching a red flashing signal, come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so. A stop sign may sometimes also be posted where this signal is located.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:
options: a:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
note: You cannot enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get completely through the intersection. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

question: If you are required to have increased insurance coverage limits but are unable to provide proof of the increased limits, you will:
options: a:Have your license and plates suspended for up to three years.,b:Only be allowed to drive on residential roads.,c:Be let off with a warning.
note: Higher insurance coverage limits will be required for a driver who has been convicted of a DUI, accumulated an excessive number of points against their license, or committed a number of other possible infractions. If the driver is not able to provide proof of the higher limits, their license and/or plates may be suspended for up to three years.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking on an incline where there is a curb, you should turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will not roll into traffic.

question: Don’t follow other cars too closely because:
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: If you follow too closely and the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid a collision.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Look for a train.,c:Be ready to stop.
note: When you see any signs indicating a nearby railroad crossing, you should slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If the red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, you must stop 15 to 50 feet before the railroad tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

question: Braking distance is affected by:
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.
note: Factors that can affect braking distance include how fast your vehicle is traveling, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
note: When approaching an intersection with a steady green traffic light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You may continue driving, but should approach the intersection at a speed that will allow you to slow down and stop if the light changes before you get there.

question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: You should look and listen for trains before crossing any railroad tracks. If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, you cannot go across the tracks. This is true even if they have no signals or the signals are not working.

question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
options: a:Before turning on your engine.,b:While backing out of your driveway.,c:When approaching speeds of 55 mph.
note: When preparing to drive, you should be sure all of your equipment is in working order. Before starting your engine, adjust all mirrors so that you can use them without having to lean forward or backward.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light is out-of-order, drivers should:
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.,b:Treat the intersection as a roundabout.,c:Drive without stopping but proceed with caution.
note: If a traffic light is out-of-order, drivers should treat the intersection as a four-way stop. The driver who arrives at the intersection first has the right-of-way.

question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
note: If another vehicle is approaching you head-on in your lane, you should first honk your horn to attract attention. If the other driver does not move over, try to escape to the right. If you swerve left and the other driver corrects at the last instant, you will still crash. If a collision is unavoidable, brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down will reduce the impact.

question: Your body gets rid of approximately:
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks an hour.,b:One alcoholic drink an hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
note: The average person’s body will process about one alcoholic drink in one hour. However, many factors play a part in determining how impaired a person will become when consuming alcohol, including the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and a person’s body weight, food intake, and general health.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On narrow roads, you must allow vehicles traveling in the opposite direction at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road. Both vehicles must have adequate space in order for the drivers to safely pass one another.

question: Pennant-shaped signs indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs usually indicate no passing zones. Text will also be on the sign to confirm that it is a no passing zone.

question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Using the outside rearview mirror.,c:Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.,d:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: You should turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
options: a:Increase,b:Maintain,c:Vary,d:Reduce.
note: When turning, you should reduce to a speed that allows you to maintain control of your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.,c:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.
note: Stopping suddenly can make it difficult for drivers behind you to avoid a rear-end collision. When stopping, release the accelerator to allow your vehicle to slow. Press the brake pedal by applying steady pressure, activating your brake lights and causing the vehicle to stop smoothly.

question: You are involved in an accident. You should:
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Help the injured.,c:Call the police.
note: If involved in an accident, you should stop your vehicle immediately. If possible, move the vehicle out of the way of traffic. Call the nearest police agency and ask for an ambulance, if necessary. Do not move the injured unnecessarily, but attempt to stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting the interstate, drivers should begin to decelerate:
options: a:As they turn on their blinker to enter the deceleration lane.,b:When they realize they are nearing their exit.,c:After turning into the deceleration lane.
note: When exiting the interstate, you must use the deceleration lane. This lane is designed to allow you to slow down before reaching the exit ramp without being a hazard to other vehicles on the freeway.

question: Bicycles on the road:
options: a:Must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.,b:Do not follow specific rules of the road.,c:Are nothing to worry about.
note: Bicycles on the road are considered vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers of motor vehicles should respect the rights of bicyclists.

question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:
options: a:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
note: Drinking coffee will not reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). While it may help you to stay awake, it cannot change your BAC or make you sober.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,d:Come to a complete stop and proceed when the way is clear.
note: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them like stop signs.

question: You are driving on a busy street and your vehicle’s accelerator sticks open. You should:
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers.
note: If your vehicle’s accelerator sticks open, your vehicle will continue to maintain its speed or accelerate, even if you remove your foot from the gas pedal. Turn off the ignition, using care to move the ignition switch only far enough to stop the engine and not engage the steering wheel locking mechanism. Apply your brakes and move off the road to a safe area.

question: When approaching a traffic signal displaying a steady green arrow, drivers:
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A green arrow displayed on a traffic signal tells drivers that they may turn in the direction of the arrow. You must be in the proper lane for such a turn. Yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally drive 10 mph over the speed limit:
options: “a:At all times.
note: c:In light traffic conditions.
column9: Speeding is against the law. You must obey the speed limit and you are responsible for knowing the speed limit when you are driving. The “speeding buffer” is a myth; you are not allowed to drive up to 10 mph over the speed limit.

question: Which of the following recommendations does not promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
note: If you look into the headlights of an oncoming vehicle, the pupil of your eye will contract. After the oncoming vehicle has passed, there will be an interval of time during which the pupil must readjust to the less intense light. During this recovery period, you are virtually driving blind.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines are used to separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed lines indicate that drivers directly next to the line are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:
options: a:You may stop to drop off passengers.,b:You may stop to look up an address.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.,d:You should never stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Instead, keep moving until you can safely pull off of the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit or where you can safely turn around.

question: You may not park:
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: There are a number of locations where it is unlawful to park, including on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the side of the road.

question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Do not affect driving abilities.,b:Help maintain driver alertness.,c:Are distracting activities.
note: Smoking while driving can create dangerous distractions by causing you to take your hands off the wheel and/or your eyes off the road.

question: If one of your tires blows out as you are driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
note: If a tire blows out while you are driving, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car headed straight down the road. Ease your foot off the gas pedal and do not apply the brakes until you have complete control. When the car is under control, brake gently and pull off the road at the nearest safe location.

question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. You should:
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your directional signal.
note: Before changing lanes, you should always verify that there are no other vehicles in the lane you want to enter by checking your mirrors and looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. You should signal every time you change lanes.

question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:
options: a:As long as an approaching train is not too close.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:If you first look carefully in both directions.,d:Under no circumstances.
note: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and/or bells at a railroad crossing mean that you must come to a complete stop. You must not go across the tracks until the lights and bells have stopped and the crossing gates are completely up. Do not drive around or under a gate that is moving up or down.

question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
note: Always signal for an appropriate amount of time before making a lane change or exiting a freeway. Before you make any move to the right or left, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over the other three?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: Directions given by traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings. People authorized to direct traffic include police officers, fire police, highway work area flag persons, and school crossing persons.

question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction. Your headlights:
options: a:Should be on their high beam setting.,b:Should be on their low beam setting.,c:Should be off. Use your parking lights.
note: Do not use your high beam headlights when approaching or following another vehicle at night. Switch to the low beam setting to ensure the safety of everyone on the road.

question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. You should:
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: If you experience a tire blowout, do not immediately apply the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and steer to remain in your traffic lane. Reduce your speed gradually by releasing the accelerator and staying off the brakes. Once you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road into a safe area.

question: Driving while being distracted by any activity:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.
note: Distractions cause drivers to react more slowly to traffic and hazards on the roadway. Distracted driving is never safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles waiting at a stop sign. If there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead have passed through the intersection, you:
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must always bring your vehicle to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding past a stop sign. Don't feel pressured by surrounding traffic to avoid making a complete stop.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:
options: a:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Accelerate quickly.
note: After stopping for a school bus that has its stop arm extended and its lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. You should always drive with caution when driving near children.

question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: Check the traffic behind you several times a minute to know if another driver is tailgating, approaching too fast, or trying to pass. If another car is following you too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end collisions are caused by vehicles following too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:
options: a:Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Has the right-of-way.,c:May force their way into traffic.
note: If you are on an entrance or acceleration ramp and are entering interstate traffic, you should yield to drivers already on the interstate highway. Merge safely into traffic when you are able to do so.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. You must stop:
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.
note: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are activated, a crossing gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or so close to the crossing that it would be hazardous to continue driving. If you are unsure if a train is too close for you to safely cross the tracks, stop. Never race a train.

question: A steady green light at an intersection means that you:
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign prohibits the turn. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians within the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic is blocking your view. You should:
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
note: You should never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and that you can safely make the turn.

question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,c:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
note: If you are involved in an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of the way of traffic, if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes as you could be struck by another vehicle. Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding can kill.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
note: As speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases. If you are moving faster than 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of living through a crash. Driving more slowly than other traffic can also be dangerous because other motorists may become impatient and make dangerous moves to pass you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Honk at the officer.
note: Traffic signals are placed at intersections to keep traffic moving and to help prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey these signals, except in instances when an officer is directing traffic.

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: a:Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine for entering and leaving your car. Before switching on the ignition, buckle your safety belt and see that all passengers do likewise.

question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and the lower part of your abdomen. Shoulder belts should sit comfortably so that you can insert your fist between the belt and your chest.

question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:
options: a:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,c:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crashes often happen when some drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Always try to drive with the flow of traffic, within the posted speed limit.

question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: A large truck has large blind spots to the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle. Avoid lingering in these areas. Because of their larger size and weight, trucks require more room to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

question: When driving near a blind pedestrian who is carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally.
note: When driving near a blind pedestrian who is carrying a white cane or walking with a guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and then proceed with caution. Be prepared to stop your vehicle in order to prevent injury or danger to the pedestrian.

question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:
options: a:Turning on your car radio.,b:Slowing down.,c:Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
note: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, you should schedule regular stops. Give yourself time to rest and stretch, even if you are not feeling tired.

question: From top to bottom, the following is the proper order for traffic lights:
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On a traffic signal arranged vertically, red is always on top and green on the bottom. When arranged horizontally, red is always on the left and green on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway:
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Before passing, you must make sure the passing lane is clear and give the proper turn signal to show you are going to change lanes.

question: Distracted drivers are at a greater risk of a crash when they are using which of the following?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Cell phone
note: Using a cell phone (including a hands-free phone) or any kind of audio device (including a radio or CD player) can be a dangerous distraction and contributes to the risk of a crash.

question: Alcohol:
options: a:Slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:Puts you to sleep.,c:Wakes you up.
note: Alcohol is a depressant drug that slows the activity of the brain and reduces the skills that you need for safe driving. Drinking alcohol results in slowed reaction time and impaired judgment.

question: If you are being followed too closely on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Speed up to match the speed of the car behind you.,b:Move into the lane to your right to let the car pass.,c:Slow down but stay in the lane.
note: If you are being followed too closely on a multilane roadway, you should move into the lane to your right when the path is clear. On multilane roads, the far left lane is intended for use by faster vehicles passing slower vehicles.

question: Distracted driving may be caused by:
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,c:Changing a radio station or CD.
note: It is estimated that drivers make 200 decisions for every mile traveled, making it vital that drivers focus their full attention on the task of driving. Performing any additional task can create a dangerous distraction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.,c:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
note: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up or try to turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

question: When driving on major highways:
options: a:Stay alert.,b:Keep your eyes moving.,c:Be ready to react to road hazards.
note: It is important to stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. To avoid "highway hypnosis," you should avoid looking at any one thing for more than a few seconds.

question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:It is more likely to be raining at night.
note: At night, your field of vision is reduced. To make sure you are able to react to hazards on the roadway, always use appropriate headlights. Drive slowly enough that you are able to stop within the distance that you can see ahead.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirements as:
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: When approaching a flashing red signal, you must stop and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track:
options: a:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,b:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.,c:Go through as soon as the train passes.
note: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not start moving as soon as a train passes. Wait until you have a clear view down all tracks before you start across. Even where there is only one track, do not start across immediately after a train passes; check again for another train that may be approaching.

question: You are involved in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. You should:
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.,b:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible. Do not leave the scene of an accident without identifying yourself and rendering assistance.

question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet roadway?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: The faster you drive on a wet roadway, the less effective your tires will be at wiping the water from the road. If your speed becomes excessive enough, your tires will lose their grip on the road entirely and you will begin to hydroplane (that is, to slide down the road on a film of water).

question: A good defensive driver:
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: Even the most experienced drivers can be distracted while driving. A defensive driver looks out for the actions of other drivers and anticipates potential problems.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive to an intersection at the same time, which one has the right-of-way when no signs or signals indicate rules?
options: a:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,b:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.
note: At an intersection of two similar roads without a traffic control device, a driver must yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.

question: It is best to keep a space cushion:
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of the vehicle.
note: To ensure that you will have time to react to hazards on the roadway, it is best to keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle. Do not crowd vehicles to your left and right sides.

question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which of the following traffic signals?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A green steady arrow means you may pass through the intersection in the direction that the arrow is pointing. Oncoming traffic is required to stop for turning traffic.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Lane usage for the motorcyclist is critical. Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: If you must drive in foggy conditions, you should use your low beam headlights, as well as your fog lights, if your vehicle has them. High beams direct their light upwards, where it can bounce off the fog and into your eyes, reducing visibility even more.

question: Highway markings:
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Highway markings provide information for drivers. Markings help drivers correctly position their vehicles on roadways, inform drivers of safe passing zones, and warn drivers about upcoming conditions.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in the area where you are driving, you should:
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in the area where you are driving, you must make every effort to give them a clear path of travel. If it is safe to do so, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to give the emergency vehicle an open pathway.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Look into the right side mirror.,c:Look into the rearview mirror.
note: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, you should look over your shoulder in the direction that you plan to move.

question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to indicate that you are turning.
options: a:Your horn,b:Your headlights,c:Hand signals
note: If your vehicle's turn signals do not work, you should use hand signals to indicate when you intend to change direction.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads. Stopping distances also increase on road surfaces covered in loose gravel or stones.

question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:
options: a:Increase their speed to reach their final destination more quickly.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: When driving on wet roads, drivers should increase their following distance.

question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. Before you start to move your car, you should:
options: a:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,b:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: When you back up a vehicle, look through your back window for pedestrians and other obstacles. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially when children are near. Before you back into or out of a driveway, get out of the vehicle and check behind your vehicle.

question: Signs indicating areas of public recreation are:
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Green.,d:Brown.
note: Signs that are brown indicate areas of cultural and historical significance or of public recreation. They can be a helpful resource when traveling in unfamiliar locations.

question: In which of the following ways can alcoholic beverages affect you?
options: a:It slows your reaction time.,b:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,c:It impairs your thinking ability.
note: Alcohol dulls the parts of your brain that control inhibition, judgment, and self-control. As a result, you may feel stimulated, lively, and a bit giddy or foolish after consuming alcohol. Alcohol also impairs your reaction time, coordination, and balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance suffers after alcohol consumption, making it difficult to react to your surroundings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: Always signal your intentions when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not allow yourself to become lazy and form the bad habit of not following this law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you drive, you're required to stop your vehicle:
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.
note: Situations where motorists are required to stop include approaching intersections with stop signs, approaching intersections where a red light is either flashing or illuminated, or any time when a traffic officer orders your vehicle to stop.

question: It is important to slow down:
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.
note: You should always slow down when driving on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or driving hazards, and when the roads are wet or slippery.

question: To avoid being in a truck or bus driver’s blind spot, you should:
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your lights at them.
note: Because a large vehicle, such as a truck or bus, has large blind spots to its sides and rear, avoid driving alongside such a vehicle and do not tailgate one.

question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.
note: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the center of the road and the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross the lines to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is a ____ line.
options: a:Broken white,b:Double solid yellow,c:Solid yellow
note: White lines separate traffic lanes traveling in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass, as long as the passing lane is clear.

question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. You should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means that you should proceed through the intersection slowly and with caution. Scan your eyes across traffic in both directions.

question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgement?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms your judgement.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgement.,c:It has no effect on either driving skills or judgement.
note: Alcohol negatively affects many skills needed for safe driving, including your reaction time and ability to see clearly. It can also harm your judgment of speed and distance, lower your inhibitions, and make you more prone to taking chances.

question: You may drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway:
options: a:As long as you aren't driving.,b:If you are riding in the back seat.,c:If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.
note: It is against the law to consume or possess any alcoholic beverage while on a public road or sidewalk. Additionally, storing an open alcoholic beverage container in an area of a motor vehicle normally occupied by the driver or passenger is prohibited on any public road.

question: Double solid yellow lines painted down the middle of the road mean:
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may not cross the lines unless you are making a left turn or passing pedestrians, bicyclists, and riders of scooters or skateboards when the opposite lane is clear and you can pass safely.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key from the ignition, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited:
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At intersections.,c:At railroad crossings.
note: Locations where it is unlawful and unsafe to pass another vehicle include hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive to an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Once the vehicle on the right has safely passed through the intersection, the other driver may proceed.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Excessive speed under the driving conditions,c:Following other vehicles too closely
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of motor vehicle crashes. Being inattentive to surroundings can cause a driver to collide with other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions are caused by drivers following other vehicles too closely.

question: A person's ability to drive can be impaired by:
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.
note: The ability to drive safely is dependent on the driver being in good physical condition. Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and being drowsy.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, the driver must produce:
options: a:Proof of insurance.,b:Their license.,c:Proof of registration.
note: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, the driver is responsible for producing their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. Drivers are required to have all three of these documents in a vehicle when it is being driven.

question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Drivers should not try to outdrive a train.

question: To prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: Your ability to handle dangerous traffic situations depends largely on searching for and identifying problems before meeting them. Looking far ahead of your vehicle does not mean you should simply stare at the center of the road. You need to continually scan the entire road, including the sides of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking facing uphill on a street that has a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. This way, if your vehicle starts to roll, it will roll into the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,b:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.
note: You cannot pass safely when driving on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal and unsafe to do so.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a:Flashing yellow,b:Steady green,c:Steady red
note: A steady yellow light on a traffic signal indicates that a steady red light will soon appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection:
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: If you arrive to an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, you should yield the right-of-way to that vehicle. You may then proceed when it is safe to do so.

question: You are coming to an intersection and have a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:
options: a:Honk your horn.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians and cars that may be caught in an intersection when you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians under every circumstance.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:
options: a:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,b:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.,c:Speed up as he or she is passing you.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should make every attempt to get out of their way. You should avoid making eye contact with a hostile driver. Challenging a hostile driver by speeding up may only make them angrier, thereby increasing their danger.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.
note: To avoid the dangers of road rage, you should never take it personally if another driver cuts you off in traffic. Just let it go and continue driving safely.

question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Expect vehicles using this emblem to be driving at speeds of 25 mph or slower.

question: Which medication(s) could have negative side effects that affect driving ability?
options: a:Any medication,b:Headache medicine,c:Diet pills
note: Any medication could potentially affect your ability to drive. Be sure to ask your doctor or pharmacist about the effects your prescription may have on driving. Read the labels on over-the-counter medicines to determine if their side effects can impair your driving.

question: The most common color of warning signs is:
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. These signs warn drivers about unexpected conditions that may not be readily apparent.

question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop before entering the intersection.,b:Yield just to the traffic on the right.,c:Yield just to the traffic on the left.,d:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection.
note: A yield sign means that you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: Fog can greatly reduce the visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,b:Not use your high beam headlights.,c:Use low beam headlights to better illuminate the road and objects.
note: Fog can greatly reduce your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive cautiously and at reduced speeds. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beams better illuminate the road and objects ahead in foggy conditions.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing
note: A flashing yellow traffic light indicates that you should drive with caution.

question: You notice a vehicle defect which may affect the safe operation of your vehicle. You should:
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,c:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.
note: Any defect that may affect the safe operation of a vehicle should be corrected as soon as possible. Defects should be corrected before the vehicle is driven.

question: The effect that lack of sleep has on your safe driving ability is the same as:
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue and being under the influence of alcohol have similar effects on your ability to drive safely. For example, being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours in a row has the same effect on your driving as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

question: If you experience a tire blowout:
options: a:Take your foot of the gas.,b:Do not immediately use your brakes.,c:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
note: If you experience a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas pedal and do not immediately apply the brakes. Gradually slow down before gently applying the brakes and pulling off the side of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When merging into traffic, you should signal and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving. Always yield to other traffic when entering a roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: After finding a parking space, checking traffic, and signaling, you should stop parallel to the vehicle directly ahead of your desired parking space before turning your wheel to park.

question: Your vehicle strikes an unattended parked vehicle and you cannot locate the vehicle’s owner. You:
options: a:Have done as much as you can.,b:Must stay until the police arrive.,c:Must leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.
note: Upon striking an unattended vehicle, stop and try to locate the owner. If you cannot find the owner, leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.

question: What is the first thing affected by alcohol consumption?
options: a:Reaction time.,b:Judgment.,c:Slurred speech.
note: Alcohol reduces all of the important skills necessary to drive safely, such as judgment, reaction time, vision, and concentration. Alcohol is absorbed into the lining of the stomach and then passes directly into the bloodstream and reaches your brain within minutes after consumption. A person’s judgment is the first thing affected after drinking an alcoholic beverage.

question: Accruing ____ points on your license within a 36-month period will result in suspension of your license for one year.
options: a:24 or more,b:21 to 23,c:18 to 20
note: Certain offenses committed while driving will count against the driver in Florida's system of suspending driver licenses. If a driver accrues 24 points or more within a 36-month period, their license will be suspended for one year.

question: When may a driver pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk?
options: a:When the vehicle does not accelerate quickly enough after the pedestrian has left the crosswalk.,b:When the pedestrian is directly in front of the vehicle.,c:When there is no visible pedestrian.
note: You are not allowed to overtake and pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk. Florida law requires that a driver assumes any vehicle stopped at a crosswalk is waiting for a crossing pedestrian, even when none can be seen at that moment.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.,c:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
note: Be prepared to reduce your speed and use caution when directed to do so by a sign, flagger, or law enforcement officer. Failure to do so is illegal and is dangerous to those working in construction zones.

question: Your chances of being in a collision begin to increase after consuming:
options: a:Four alcoholic drinks.,b:Three alcoholic drinks.,c:Two alcoholic drinks.
note: If you drink alcohol, even just one drink, your chances of being in a crash are much greater than if you did not drink any alcohol. No one can drink alcohol and drive safely, even if you have been driving for many years.

question: Drowsy drivers:
options: a:Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.,b:Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,c:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsiness can make people drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to make a drowsy driver alert to roadway hazards.

question: When driving in fog:
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your low beams.,c:Use your high beams.
note: You should use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not functioning due to a power outage:
options: a:Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.,b:Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.,d:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
note: If a traffic light at an intersection is not functioning due to a power outage, yield to other drivers in the same manner as you would when approaching a four-way stop. When it is your turn, proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: You are driving on the roadway and hear a siren behind you. You should:
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When you hear the siren or see the flashing lights of an emergency vehicle coming from behind your vehicle, you must create a clear path for the emergency vehicle and stop. Reduce your speed and safely pull over to the side of the road. If the emergency vehicle is directly behind your vehicle when you are in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of its way.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.,c:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
note: Be prepared to reduce your speed and use caution when directed to do so by a sign, crossing guard, or law enforcement officer. Always drive with extra caution in a school zone.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash:
options: a:Stop.,b:Call the police.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: If you are involved in a crash, move your vehicle off of the road and stop, if possible. If anyone is injured, call 911 and provide appropriate help. You must report the crash to law enforcement if there is an injury, a death, and/or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 worth of damage made to non-vehicle government property, such as signs or guardrails).

question: If a gate near a drawbridge is about to lower across the road:
options: a:Find a way around the gate.,b:Quickly drive under the lowering gate.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait for the gate to rise before you proceed.
note: Many drawbridges have gates with flashing red lights and bells. Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers across your lane. Not only is it against the law to drive around or under a crossing gate, it is extremely dangerous.

question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,b:Use tires with proper air pressure.,c:Replace tires with bad tread.
note: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle glides on top of a thin layer of water between its tires and the road. Tires with low air pressure or bad tread can increase the risk of hydroplaning. Speeding also increases the risk.

question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:
options: a:Is used only on one-way streets.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular green traffic light, but traffic must turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Means that you may proceed, but only if the green arrow is accompanied by a circular green light.
note: A green arrow has the same meaning as a circular green traffic light, but traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:
options: a:No special action is required.,b:The driver should honk their horn.,c:The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.,d:Slow down and pass the animal carefully.
note: Be very cautious any time you encounter an animal on the roadway. Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling or frightening it.

question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Slow down.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop whenever you see pedestrians walking on or crossing the roadway. Be particularly careful where children are present. Always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing in a crosswalk.

question: Children are required to wear their seat belts:
options: a:Anytime they are in a moving car.,b:If their parents think they should.,c:If they choose to do so.
note: Florida law requires that a fastened seat belt must be worn in all motor vehicles on public roadways by the driver and passengers in the front seat. All children under the age of 18 are also required to wear their fastened seat belts, regardless of where they are seated in the vehicle.

question: If you are involved in a crash with an unattended vehicle, you:
options: a:May leave the scene without attempting to make contact with the vehicle's owner.,b:Must contact the vehicle's owner or leave a note.,c:Must stay near the vehicle until its owner comes to move it.
note: If you are involved in a crash with a vehicle that is unattended, you must make every effort to contact the vehicle's owner and notify law enforcement. If you are not able to find the owner, you can leave a note with your name, contact information, and license plate number.

question: You are driving when it starts to sleet or snow. You should:
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.,b:Allow additional distance between your vehicle and the vehicles that you are following.,c:Approach all vehicles with caution.
note: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance when driving in wet and cold weather because a slippery road surface will increase the distance needed for your vehicle to stop.

question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:
options: a:Make no driving errors.,b:Have trouble driving slowly.,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,d:Have trouble staying in their lane and controlling their vehicle.
note: Choosing to eat, drink, or smoke while driving is dangerous because these actions require a driver to remove their hands from the wheel and their eyes from the road. Drivers who engage in distracting activities while driving have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

question: Certain highway signs require drivers to obey an indicated instruction. Such signs are known as:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs require drivers to obey an indicated instruction. Failure to comply is subject to penalty.

question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:There is a larger volume of traffic at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night.
note: Because it is dark, drivers cannot see as well at night as they can during the day. From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, or at any other time when persons or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, drivers must use their headlights.

question: When passing a large vehicle, the driver of a small vehicle must be prepared for:
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
note: Large vehicles can cause wind gusts with a force great enough to cause direction changes in smaller vehicles. Drivers of small vehicles should be prepared to take proper corrective steering action when approaching or passing large vehicles that are moving at or near maximum speeds.

question: When approaching a traffic signal displaying a flashing yellow arrow, drivers:
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should come to a complete stop.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow indicates that left turns are allowed in the direction of the arrow. However, the oncoming traffic has a green light and you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:
options: a:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: If there is an available passing lane, you may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning left or waiting to turn left. It is also legal to pass on the right when driving on a multilane road with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction. You may never drive off the pavement or main-traveled portion of the road to pass another vehicle.

question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear the signal of an approaching emergency vehicle. You should:
options: a:Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
note: If you hear the siren or see the flashing lights of an emergency vehicle, you must slow down, provide a clear path for the vehicle, and stop. Don't try to outdrive the emergency vehicle.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,b:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
note: If you are stopped by the police, keep your hands on the wheel and ask any passengers to keep their hands in view as well. You should remain in the vehicle unless the police officer asks you to get out. Wait until the officer asks you to retrieve your driver license, registration, and insurance cards.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:
options: a:Slows down your reactions.,b:Makes you feel less confident.,c:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
note: As alcohol builds up in your system, it will slow your reactions, make you feel more confident, and cause you to make more errors.

question: To change lanes you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,b:Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, you should activate your turn signal in the appropriate direction and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move in order to check your blind spot and check the far lane to be sure no one else is trying to enter the same lane as you. Change lanes when you are sure it is safe to do so.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.,b:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.,c:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
note: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross a road or street. Crosswalks may be marked by horizontal lines, vertical lines, or a combination of the two. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing other vehicles:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing another vehicle, check your mirrors and blind spots. Before changing lanes, activate the appropriate turn signal. Re-enter the lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action is to:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Apply the brakes sharply to stop.,c:Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.,d:Slow down and prepare to stop before entering the intersection.
note: A steady yellow traffic light indicates that the light will soon change to red. You should be prepared to stop for the red light, if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A “No standing” sign at a certain location means:
options: a:You may never stop your vehicle there.,b:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.,c:You may stop temporarily only to pickup or discharge passengers.
note: A "No standing" sign means that you may only make a temporary stop to load or discharge passengers.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is to:
options: a:Get out of the car and go for help.,b:Lay down in your car and go to sleep.,c:Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
note: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is stay in your car and wait for help. You are most likely to be found if you don't leave your vehicle. Additionally, it may be unsafe to walk around outside in a snowstorm.

question: When driving in a low-visibility situation, you should:
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive as if it is a high-visibility situation.
note: Increase your following distance in low-visibility situations. It will be more difficult to see what the car in front of you is doing and you may need extra time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may park or stop along the shoulder of the freeway:
options: a:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,b:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,c:If you need to look at a map for directions.,d:Only in an emergency situation.
note: It is prohibited to park on the shoulder of a freeway, except in an emergency.

question: If you need to slow down while driving on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: To slow down on a slippery road, you should first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down even more, gently apply a slow, steady pressure to your brake pedal.

question: Your first response to reduced visibility should be:
options: a:Turning on your headlights.,b:Reducing your speed.,c:Turning on your windshield wipers.
note: Reducing your speed should be your first response to decreased visibility and dangerous road conditions.

question: While driving on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, you encounter a bicyclist traveling in the same direction. What is the safest way to pass the bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and wait until there is no traffic approaching, then pass the bicyclist while leaving him or her sufficient space.,b:Continue driving straight. It is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.,c:Do not pass the bicyclist until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: You should pass a bicyclist the same way you would pass any other vehicle, but not so fast or close to them that you throw debris in their face or blow them around with the draft of air from your vehicle. Allow at least 3 feet of space between your side mirror and the bicyclist, or at least 5 feet on higher speed roads or when there is a group of bicyclists. Honking unnecessarily may startle riders and make them more likely to crash.

question: You may drive across a dashed white line:
options: a:At any time.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe to change lanes.
note: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by broken white lines. You may cross over dashed lines to pass, if it is safe to do so.

question: You notice that the driver in the vehicle ahead of you is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:
